steps.title: 01-open: Open http://127.0.0.1:3000 in the browser. If a login page appears, sign in with username 'admin' and password 'admin'; if Grafana prompts to change the admin password, skip it. Then find and open the provisioned dashboard named 'Service health' (use the search/Dashboards page). Report the exact titles of all panels on that dashboard, exactly as displayed, one per line.

02-create: In Grafana at http://127.0.0.1:3000, create a NEW dashboard. Add a visualization panel of type 'Stat' (not the default time series). Set the panel title to exactly '{{runid}} Availability'. Set the panel's data source to the 'TestData' data source (choose it in the query data source picker; leave the default scenario). Then save the dashboard with the title exactly '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard' (use Save dashboard from the save icon, enter the name, confirm). Verify afterwards that the dashboard is saved (no unsaved-changes indicator) and that the Stat panel titled '{{runid}} Availability' is visible with the TestData data source. Report the dashboard's URL from the browser address bar and the panel title as shown.

03-open: In Grafana at http://127.0.0.1:3000, open the dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard. Enter edit mode (Edit dashboard). Add a new panel of type 'Text' (add a new visualization and choose the Text panel type). Set its title to exactly '{{runid}} Notes' and set its text content to include the runid '{{runid}}' (e.g. 'Bench notes for run {{runid}}'). Then save the dashboard (Save dashboard, confirm). Verify afterwards that the dashboard is saved (no unsaved-changes indicator) and that a Text panel titled '{{runid}} Notes' is visible on the dashboard showing the runid in its rendered content. Report the panel title and the rendered text content as shown on the page.

04-open: In Grafana at http://127.0.0.1:3000, open the dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard. Do two things and save them together: (1) Add the tag 'bench' to the dashboard (via Dashboard settings > General > Tags, add 'bench'). (2) Set the dashboard's time range to the last 6 hours (open the time picker in the top bar and choose 'Last 6 hours'). Then save the dashboard via the save icon, and in the save dialog TICK the 'Update default time range' checkbox so the 6-hour range is persisted into the saved dashboard, then confirm the save. Verify afterwards: reload the dashboard page fresh and confirm the tag 'bench' appears (e.g. in the dashboard breadcrumb/search or settings) and the time picker shows 'Last 6 hours' after reload. Report the tag and the time range shown after a fresh reload.

05-open: In Grafana at http://127.0.0.1:3000, open the dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard. Set the dashboard's auto-refresh interval to '1m': open the time picker (top-right, the refresh interval selector next to the time range) and choose '1m' from the auto-refresh interval options. Then persist it: if the dashboard now shows unsaved changes, save the dashboard (Save dashboard, confirm; tick 'Update default time range' only if offered and relevant). Then reload the dashboard page fresh (plain URL http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard) and verify the auto-refresh interval still shows '1m' in the top bar (the refresh button/label). Report the auto-refresh interval value shown after the fresh reload, and whether a save was needed/performed.

06-open: In Grafana at http://127.0.0.1:3000, open the dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard in a fresh load (view mode, not edit). Verify and report: (1) the exact URL shown in the browser address bar; (2) the dashboard title shown; (3) the titles of all panels visible; (4) the time range shown in the top bar; (5) the auto-refresh interval shown in the top bar; (6) open Dashboard settings > General and report the tags listed for this dashboard (confirm whether 'bench' is present); (7) confirm the Stat panel '{{runid}} Availability' uses the TestData data source (open its panel editor if needed). Report each of these as concrete values read from the page.
